title: kv-cache-attention-kernel-seqlen-breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for reproducing and debugging odd behaviour when sequence lengths cross 2048/4096 thresholds. Focus: KV cache behavior + attention kernel selection (cuBLAS vs fused attention vs custom kernel) + edge-case regression after quantization/packing changes

Summary of symptoms (observed on dedicated-local, RTX A6000 pool):
- At seqlen ~4097 we see sudden latency spike (~3-5x) and occasional token-level output stutter.
- In some requests KV cache appears partially invalidated: cached KV size != expected (log shows KV entries for earlier tokens, then a partial overwrite).
- Kernel selection log indicates fallback to slower generic kernel when seqlen > 4096 or when attention_mode toggles.
- No persistent OOM, but intermittent cudaLaunch failures: "CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED" in logs around step where cache read happens.

What I ran (commands + saved outputs):
1) baseline repro (python):
   PYTHONPATH=./python:./build python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model redwood-small --batch 1 --seqlen 4096 --prompt len=4000 --steps 50 2>&1 | tee repro_4096.log
   - runtime: normal (~120ms/token)
   - kernel selection: fused_attention (fast), KV size as expected

2) cross boundary repro:
   PYTHONPATH=./python:./build python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model redwood-small --batch 1 --seqlen 4100 --prompt len=4000 --steps 50 2>&1 | tee repro_4100.log
   - latency jump to ~380ms/token at the moment token index > 4096
   - log snippet: "kernel_selector: selected generic_attention_kernel (reason: seqlen>4096)"
   - intermittent "cudaLaunchKernel failed: unknown error" at internal attention compute call

3) KV cache focused run (with verbose KV tracing):
   export RUNTIME_KV_DEBUG=1; python tools/kv_trace.py --model redwood-small --seqlen 4100 --steps 80 | tee kv_trace_4100.log
   - observed: KV write at step 1023 succeeded; subsequent read at step 1024 returned a smaller tensor (shape mismatch).
   - log excerpt: "KVCache::read: expected (num_heads=32, seq=4100, head_dim=64) got (num_heads=32, seq=1024, head_dim=64)"
   - hypothesis: buffer wrapping/aliasing bug in cache resize when kernel changes lane/block size

4) Quantized/packed model run (8-bit transposed packing enabled):
   python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model redwood-small-8bit --pack-transpose true --seqlen 4100 2>&1 | tee repro_4100_8bit.log
   - Kernel selection fell back earlier (around seqlen 2049) to generic kernel
   - Observed slightly different KV shapes in logs (pack step altered expected layout)

Relevant log snippets (copied):
- "[2026-02-27T15:12:43Z] kernel_selector: candidate fused_attn (max_seq=4096) rejected: exceeds max_seq -> select generic_attention_kernel"
- "[2026-02-27T15:12:43Z] KVCache::resize: new_capacity=8192 previous=4096 (triggered by seqlen growth)"
- "[2026-02-27T15:12:44Z] KVCache::write idx=4095 len=1 -> ok"
- "[2026-02-27T15:12:44Z] KVCache::read idx=4096 returned_len=1024 (mismatch)"
- "[2026-02-27T15:12:44Z] attention_kernel: launch generic_attention_kernel grid=(...) block=(...) -> cudaLaunchKernel returned CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED"

Hypotheses (ordered):
1) Kernel-selection boundary: fused attention kernels are compiled/optimized for max_seq=4096. When seqlen crosses threshold, selector switches to generic kernel which expects different KV layout/packing; cache resize happens but stride/layout assumptions not reconciled -> partial reads.
2) KV cache resize logic has a race with in-flight kernels: resize allocates new buffer + pointer swap; if kernel_selector changes concurrently, a kernel may read old pointer with new indexing logic -> shape mismatch or out-of-bounds read leading to launch failure.
3) Packing/quantization modifies memory layout (packed transposed blocks) which fused kernels assume; when fallback occurs the generic kernel interprets packed layout as normal -> garbage reads.
4) Edge-case in ring buffer wrap index math: code path for wrap assumes bucket size aligned to 1024 tokens; crossing 4096 boundary triggers different alignment rounding -> partial overwrite at high sequences.

Immediate repro checklist for eng-sre/serving-runtime: (what to run locally)
- Reproduce with sanitizers: build with ASAN/UBSAN on CPU (if possible) and cuda-memcheck for GPU runs.
- Add additional KVCache fence/sync around resize to prevent in-flight kernel read of old pointer. Quick patch: KVCache::resize -> cudaDeviceSynchronize() before pointer swap (test perf impact).
- Add invariant checks: after resize, validate KVCache->stride/head_dim/num_heads against kernel_selector expectations (log fatal if mismatch).
- Re-run quantized pipeline and assert pack layout header metadata present and validated before kernel dispatch.
- Add unit test that simulates crossing the boundary: append tokens until seqlen = 4096 -> 4100 in rapid succession while busy computing.

Notes on config & env (to reproduce environment):
- CUDA 12.1, NVIDIA driver 535.86.10, CUDNN 9.0 beta locally used by runtime
- PyTorch 2.2 build for A6000 (but serving runtime uses its own CUDA kernels, minimal PyTorch involvement)
- Commit refs: runtime @ 3f2b7c1 (PR 1298 merged 2026-02-18), kernel selector changes (PR 1279), kv-cache resizing logic from PR 1246
- Machine: dedicated-local-a6000-2 (2 GPUs), batch size 1 for repros, small model (redwood-small) to keep trace logs concise

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the fused_attention kernel compiled with a hard-coded max_seq macro? Check build artifacts for MAX_SEQ constants.
- Are pack/transpose metadata headers present in KV buffers? If not, introduce a tiny header struct with magic/version to avoid misinterpretation by fallback kernel.
- Re-run with NVTX ranges to correlate kernel dispatches with cache ops and ensure ordering.
- Check if earlier perf-opt PR changed default alignment from 256 -> 1024 causing wrap math bug (look at PR 1210).

Short-term mitigation options (customer-impacting):
- Force kernel_selector to prefer generic kernel for all seqlen when pack-transpose enabled (safer correctness, slower)
- Add temporary guard: deny seqlen > 4096 for optimized/fused kernels with clear error message to user asking to use smaller tokens or use dedicated config (document in release notes)

Next steps (who/when):
- Today: add validation logs + assert on KV layout mismatch (Maya)
- Tomorrow: patch KVCache::resize to synchronize and run cuda-memcheck across repros (Ethan)
- Thurs: test quantized flow and add header magic for packed layout (Lina)
- Fri: consider temporary runtime flag to disable fused kernels for pack-transpose models until fix is in (release/ops)

References / eyeballs: please ping @ethan, @lina, @mike-k (serving-runtime) if you have context on recent alignment/packing PRs.

Quick copy-paste log for PR thread:
---
kernel_selector: selected generic_attention_kernel (reason: seqlen>4096)
KVCache::resize: new_capacity=8192 previous=4096 (triggered by seqlen growth)
KVCache::read idx=4096 returned_len=1024 (mismatch)
attention_kernel: cudaLaunchKernel -> CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED
---

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a formal incident runbook if the hypothesis about resize race/pack-layout is confirmed.
